chunks: It was also narrated by Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb al-Kulaynī, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from some of his companions, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created the world in six days, then reduced them from the days of the year, and the year is three hundred and fifty-four days. Shaʿbān is never complete, and the month of Ramaḍān never decreases, by Allah, ever; and an obligation is never deficient.
Indeed Allah, Exalted is He, says: “And that you complete the number.”
And Shawwāl is twenty-nine days, and Dhū al-Qaʿdah is thirty days.
Because of the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “And We appointed for Mūsā thirty nights, and We completed them with ten, so the appointed term of his Lord was completed as forty nights.”
And Dhū al-Ḥijjah is twenty-nine days, and al-Muḥarram is thirty days; then after that, the months are one complete month and one deficient month.

This report also resembles what has preceded, in that it is not sound to argue by it, for the same reasons we have already mentioned: namely, that it is a solitary report that yields neither knowledge nor practice, and that the apparent meaning of the Qur’an and the mutawātir reports are not opposed by the like of it. Also, its wording and meanings differ while the report is one. Moreover, it contains reasoning that reveals that it was not established from an Imam of guidance عليه السلام. Among that is that His saying, Exalted is He, “And We appointed for Mūsā thirty nights,” does not necessitate the perpetual completeness of a similar month in Dhū al-Qaʿdah. The coincidence of Dhū al-Qaʿdah being complete in the days of Mūsā عليه السلام does not require its completeness in future times, nor does it indicate that it had always been like that in the past. If that is so, then attributing an everlasting rationale for the completeness of Dhū al-Qaʿdah to what the Qur’an included of its being complete at one time is invalid as a truthful report from Allah, Mighty and Majestic—especially since it is also offered as a rationale for the completeness of the month of Ramaḍān, though there is no relation between them in mention of completeness. The deduction of six days from the year does not prevent deficiency from occurring in two or three consecutive months, nor the completeness of three or four consecutive months. So how can reasoning be sound through something that neither intellect, nor custom, nor language necessitates? Likewise, the reasoning that the month of Ramaḍān is thirty days because obligations are not deficient is unsound, for the deficiency of the month from thirty days does not necessitate deficiency in the obligation of acting within it. It has been established that Allah, Exalted is He, has not bound us to perform the acts of the days themselves, nor is it sound that we be charged with performing time itself. Rather, He has bound us to actions in the days and to acts by means of time. Thus, the deficiency of one span of time in relation to another is not thereby a deficiency in the action. Do you not see that whoever has an act made obligatory upon him in a specified month, and performs it in that month according to what was set for him—from its beginning at its first, to his completing it at its last—has completed what was obligatory upon him, even if the month is deficient from full length? The Muslims have unanimously agreed that a woman observing a waiting period by months, if her husband divorces her at the beginning of a month and she completes three months in which one is complete at thirty days and two are each twenty-nine days, then she has fulfilled Allah’s obligation upon her in the ʿiddah in full, without deficiency. The deficiency of the two months does not transfer to the obligation therein upon the woman in the waiting period, as we have stated. And if a person were to vow to fast for Allah, Exalted is He, a month following the month of his return from travel or recovery from illness, and it happened that the following month was twenty-nine days, then if he fasted it from its beginning to its end, he would have fulfilled Allah’s obligation therein completely, and the deficiency of the month would not imply deficiency in the obligation he performed within it. Likewise, the argument that the month of Ramaḍān can only be thirty days by His saying, Exalted is He, “And that you complete the number,” is invalid as something established from an Imam of guidance, due to what we mentioned concerning the completeness of an obligation performed in months that are less than thirty days. Along with this, the apparent meaning of the Qur’an indicates that the command to complete the number was directed only to the meaning of making up what was missed of the fast.

As Allah, Exalted is He, says: “So whoever among you witnesses the month, let him fast it; and whoever is ill or on a journey, then a number of other days. Allah desires ease for you and does not desire hardship for you, and that you complete the number.”

So Allah, Exalted is He, informed that He made obligatory upon the traveler and the sick person, when they break the fast during travel, to make it up in other days so that by that they may complete the number of what they missed from fasting the month that has passed. There is in that no specification of what number the make-up is based on; rather, it is a command regarding the make-up of what was missed, whatever that may be. This discussion that we have mentioned indicates that the reasoning cited for the month of Ramaḍān being a full thirty days is fabricated and not soundly transmitted from the Imams عليهم السلام. Even if the hadith were free of all that we have mentioned, the wording of its matn would still not necessitate acting contrary to the lunar crescents. That is because denying the claim of the generality that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم fasted the month of Ramaḍān twenty-nine days more often than he fasted it thirty days does not prevent the possibility that he may have fasted it twenty-nine days, except that his fasting it thus was less frequent than his fasting it thirty days. Even if his fasting صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم during the period in which it was obligatory upon him in his lifetime was thirty days, that would not prevent a change of state in that regard and its being, at some times, twenty-nine days, according to what we have previously stated concerning that. The statement after that that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم only fasted it complete does not establish that the month of fasting is thirty days in every case, because the fast is other than the month: it is the act of the fasting person; while the month is the motions of the celestial sphere, and that is the act of Allah, Exalted is He. The description of completeness applies only to the fast, which is the act of the servant, not to the description of time, which is the act of Allah, Exalted is He. We have already clarified that previously. Using His saying, Exalted is He, “And that you complete the number,” as proof does not necessitate what the advocates of fixed numbering supposed—namely, that the month of Ramaḍān cannot be twenty-nine days—because completing the count of a deficient month by acting throughout all of it is like completing the count of a complete month by acting throughout the rest of it; no rational person differs concerning that. As for the separate statement that Shawwāl is twenty-nine days, it does not support what they said; rather, the report may mean that it is like that at certain times, not that it must be so in every case. Likewise, the statement that Dhū al-Qaʿdah is thirty days and never deficient—its meaning is what we mentioned: not that it can never be deficient in any sense, such that it could not at times be complete. Supporting that with His saying, Exalted is He, “And We appointed for Mūsā thirty nights,” confirms this interpretation, because it indicates its occurrence in a certain time among times, which the Qur’an mentioned as thirty days. Thus it follows that it is not never deficient absolutely; rather, it may be complete, even though deficiency is also possible for it. And what indicates the possibility of deficiency in Dhū al-Qaʿdah at some times...

key_terms.الْأَخْبَارِ الْمُتَوَاتِرَةِ: mass-transmitted reports that carry stronger evidentiary force
key_terms.الْأَهِلَّةِ: the lunar crescents that determine the actual beginning and end of months
key_terms.الْعِدَّةَ: the required count or number to be completed, particularly in relation to missed fasts
key_terms.الْفَرَائِضَ: the obligatory acts prescribed by Allah, whose validity is not negated by a shorter month
key_terms.الْقَضَاءِ: making up missed acts of worship, here specifically missed fasts
key_terms.خَبَرٌ وَاحِدٌ: a solitary report that does not establish certainty on its own
key_terms.ذُو الْقَعْدَةِ: the month discussed in connection with the verse about Mūsā عليه السلام
key_terms.شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ: the month of fasting under discussion, especially regarding whether it may be twenty-nine or thirty days

ai.seo_question: Does the phrase “and that you complete the number” prove that the month of Ramaḍān must always be thirty days?
ai.summary: This passage presents a report about the lengths of lunar months, especially Ramaḍān, and then critically examines it. The text argues that the report cannot override the apparent Qur’an, mutawātir reports, and rational principles, and explains that completing the fast means fulfilling the obligation within whatever number of days the month actually contains, whether twenty-nine or thirty.
